h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: Upgrading an existing 1x1 conv to 3x3 only adds receptive field, so it gains less than replacing none, skip or pool on edge 0.
With edge 4 cut, node 1 reaches the output only indirectly via edges 2 and 5, so improving edge 0 is partially masked.
A residual shortcut is most valuable alongside a deep conv path into the output, mirroring ResNet-style cells.
Replacing the beneficial input-to-output shortcut with a conv destroys the residual path, so the gain is smaller than when replacing none or pool.
A strong parallel conv into node 3 compensates through summation for losing conv capacity on edge 5.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is zero, so a conv on edge 4 processes no signal and the edit is nearly null.
Adding a new identity input to the output is gain-of-function, whereas the same edit replacing a conv is loss-of-function.
Removing edge 5 when edge 3 is already absent leaves the output fed only by edge 4, or by nothing at all.
With edge 5 cut, node 2 is disconnected from the output, so improving edge 1 has almost no effect.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is zero, so a conv on edge 2 processes no signal and contributes nothing.
